chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Erroll Garner in Pittsburgh and Jimmy Blanton
summary: Collins recalls first seeing Garner at a Pittsburgh club wiping his brow every eight bars, and seeing Jimmy Blanton on a riverboat.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Had Earl Garner recorded a lot then?

Well yes, he'd recorded -- you know he was with the Slam Stewart trio before that, before I joined him Earl was with Slam before -- let's see, who followed Earl. Billy Taylor. Errol was with Slam and the Slam Stewart before then. So he had quite a bit of exposure.

Yeah, I had seen -- the first time I'd seen Earl, my impression of Earl -- here I'm with Fletcher again. I went to -- Earl was from Pittsburgh, and we played Pittsburgh this night, and I went to a club and there was this little guy, this funny looking little man, this little funny looking genius sitting here playing. And the one thing -- another thing that impressed me about his playing was he wiped his brow every eight bars. You know, it was -- I'd count the
bars. You know, he's a showman too, you know. You know, he had his hankerchief right here and the eighth bar he'd grab it and wipe his forehead and get into this intricate piano again.

Never eight bars. But I also during that time I saw Blanton, Jimmy Blanton. He was in Pittsburgh. He was working one of the showboats, what do you call up and down the river, you know. He was working on this boat with a man by the name of Fate Marble. They were coming from St. Louis. But I had met Blanton before, in St. Louis, when I was with Roy. But he was then in Pittsburgh at this time. This is just before he went with Duke. But he was also -- he was a monster, you know. Those were good days, you know, very good days. But this is the first time I met Errol was at this little club called the Ritz Club, and he was just something else. But as I say, in addition to his playing he was very agile with that handkerchief, you know. But any way, after we -- Beryl left Slam. Beryl rejoined us. Have you ever heard anything that Barrel has done?
No? Well, she's quite a pianist. Art loved her, you know. But Art loved anybody good. If you could play he loved you. You know. And I'm -- let's see
